steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to enable component creation and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you the foundation to create a React component and manage state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. Please import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the SecretsCompliance component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named SecretsCompliance that returns an empty fragment initially.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name 'SecretsCompliance' and have it return an empty fragment using <> and </>.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react'

// Create the SecretsCompliance component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named SecretsCompliance is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: The component is named 'SecretsCompliance' and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the SecretsCompliance component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'SecretsCompliance' and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing or incorrectly defined. Check the name and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize secrets state
steps.instruction: Inside the SecretsCompliance component, initialize a state variable called 'secrets' using useState. Set its initial value to an array containing at least two sample secret objects with properties like 'name', 'type', and 'value' (e.g., API keys, database passwords).
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to declare a state variable. The initial value should be an array of objects representing sensitive data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'secrets' initialized with sample secret data, ready to be displayed or manipulated in later steps.
successCriteria: The 'secrets' state variable is declared using useState with an initial array containing at least two secret objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the secrets state with sample sensitive data. This sets up the foundation for managing and displaying compliance-related information.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'secrets' is declared with useState and its initial value is an array of objects representing secrets (like API keys or passwords).
steps.feedbackWrong: The secrets state isn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState to declare 'secrets' with an initial array of secret objects.

steps.title: Initialize compliance state
steps.instruction: Inside your SecretsCompliance component, initialize a state variable called 'isCompliant' using useState with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false and destructure the returned array into isCompliant and setIsCompliant.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a boolean state variable
const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable isCompliant initialized to false, ready to track compliance status.
successCriteria: The component includes a useState call for isCompliant with initial value false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the compliance state. This boolean will track whether the secrets meet compliance requirements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value and destructuring into isCompliant and setIsCompliant.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add a useState call inside the component to create the isCompliant state variable with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Create compliance check handler
steps.instruction: Inside the SecretsCompliance component, define a function called 'checkCompliance' that validates if secrets are properly masked and updates isCompliant state.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if secrets are masked (e.g., contains '***') and sets isCompliant accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named checkCompliance is defined inside the component, ready to validate secrets and update compliance state.
successCriteria: The checkCompliance function is defined inside the SecretsCompliance component and updates isCompliant based on secret masking validation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the compliance check handler. This function will validate whether secrets are properly masked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'checkCompliance' and is defined inside the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The compliance check handler isn't properly defined. Ensure you create a function called 'checkCompliance' inside the component.

steps.title: Create secret masking handler
steps.instruction: Inside your SecretsCompliance component, define a function called 'maskSecrets' that takes the current secrets array and returns a new array where each secret's value is replaced with asterisks (e.g., '**********') to protect sensitive data.
steps.hint: Create a function that maps over the secrets array and returns a new array with masked values. You can use the map method and replace each value with a string of asterisks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a maskSecrets function that can create a safe display version of secrets by replacing actual values with asterisks.
successCriteria: A function named maskSecrets is defined that takes an array and returns a new array with masked values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the secret masking handler. This function is essential for protecting sensitive data when displaying it in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your maskSecrets function properly maps over the secrets array and returns a new array with masked values (using asterisks).
steps.feedbackWrong: The maskSecrets function isn't quite right. Remember it should take the secrets array and return a new array where each secret's value is replaced with asterisks to hide sensitive information.

steps.title: Add component structure with header
steps.instruction: Return a container div with a header element containing the title 'Secrets & Compliance Management' from your component.
steps.hint: Replace the 'return null;' statement with JSX that includes a div and an h1 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div containing an h1 with the specified title.
successCriteria: The component returns JSX with a div wrapper and an h1 element containing 'Secrets & Compliance Management'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've built the basic UI structure with a clear header.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a div containing an h1 with the exact title 'Secrets & Compliance Management'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you replaced the return statement with a div and h1 containing the correct title.

steps.title: Display secrets list
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a section that maps through the masked secrets and displays each secret's name and masked value in list items.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the secrets array to generate a list of JSX elements. Each item should show the secret's name and its masked value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of secrets with their names and masked values when rendered.
successCriteria: The secrets list section is added and correctly maps through the secrets array to display each secret's name and masked value in list items.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the secrets list section that displays each secret's name and masked value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a list section, but make sure you're mapping through the secrets array and displaying both the name and masked value for each secret.
steps.feedbackWrong: The secrets list section is missing or not correctly implemented. Check that you're using map on the secrets array and displaying each secret's properties.

steps.title: Add compliance status display
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current compliance status. Use the isCompliant state variable to show 'Compliant' when true and 'Not Compliant' when false.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or conditional rendering to display different text based on the isCompliant state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing either 'Compliant' or 'Not Compliant' based on the current isCompliant state value.
successCriteria: The paragraph element displays the correct compliance status text using the isCompliant state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the compliance status display that shows the current compliance state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your paragraph uses the isCompliant state variable to conditionally show 'Compliant' or 'Not Compliant'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The compliance status display isn't working correctly. Check that you're using the isCompliant state variable and displaying the appropriate text based on its value.

steps.title: Add compliance check button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Check Compliance' inside the component's return structure, and wire its onClick event to the checkCompliance handler function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the compliance status paragraph. Use the onClick attribute to call your handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Check Compliance' button appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the compliance validation logic.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Check Compliance' is present in the return structure, and its onClick event is correctly wired to the checkCompliance handler function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the compliance check button and wired it to the handler. This completes the interactive dashboard for secrets and compliance validation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Check Compliance' and its onClick event calls the checkCompliance function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a <button> element with onClick={checkCompliance} and the text 'Check Compliance'.
